note: Adapted from Light & Wilson 1936, original in English (The nasute termites of the Philippines, The Philippine Journal of Science 60: 461–520). Both the alate and the worker are given as Unknown in the original. Only two lots, each containing one soldier, collected at Paete, Laguna Province, Luzon (collected by McGregor), were received from Oshima as autotypes of N. gracilis and clearly disagree with Oshima's original description; the authors consider that they may come from a southern island and were misplaced during handling, and that the two lots may be from the same nest. The species name honours Masamitsu Oshima, a pioneer of Philippine termite research. Fig. 15 (soldier head in dorsal and lateral view, left mandible) not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Belongs to the brown-headed matangensis group and is closest to N. panayensis: much smaller in size, hind tibia much shorter, abdominal tergites unpigmented. Type locality Paete, Laguna Province, Luzon; the only nasute termite of this group known from Luzon.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head pale orange-brown, paler posteriorly; middle of the nasus darker; abdominal tergites almost unpigmented. Head and nasus shape as in Fig. 15 a, b, very similar to N. panayensis but smaller; base of the nasus slightly thicker than in the latter. Mandibles as in Fig. 15 b. Antennae pale yellow, 12-segmented, slightly shorter than head plus nasus. Measurements (mm and indices, from type collection No. 1509, a typical soldier from Laguna): head plus nasus 1.47; head length (excluding nasus) 0.90; nasus length 0.57; head projection 0.24; head height 0.60; head width 0.90; fore tibia length 0.78; head index 1.00; head-nasus index 0.63; head projection index 0.27; leg extension index 0.87.
